paragraphs.text: In spring, many songbirds begin singing before sunrise, producing a burst of sound known as the dawn chorus. Although the phenomenon is familiar, scientists still disagree about why it happens at this particular time of day.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: One explanation concerns sound. In the early morning the air is usually calm and cool, and some researchers argue that song travels further then than at any other time. However, measurements in several forests have found only small differences in how far sound carries.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A second idea is that dawn is simply a poor time for feeding. Insects are less active in the cold, and low light makes food hard to find, so birds may use the time for singing instead. Birds given extra food the evening before have been observed to sing earlier and for longer the next morning.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Singing may also be a way of showing strength. A male that has survived a cold night and still has the energy to sing loudly is sending a message to rivals and to females. This would explain why singing is most intense in the breeding season.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Artificial light may be changing the chorus. In several European cities, birds living near street lamps begin singing earlier than those in darker areas, although it is not yet clear whether this affects their breeding success.
paragraphs.label: E

items.prompt: a suggestion that singing gives information about a bird’s physical condition
research that did not fully support one theory
a human influence on the timing of bird song
an experiment in which the birds’ food supply was changed
a mention of continuing disagreement among scientists

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. The reading passage has five paragraphs, A–E. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–E.
